title: Altitude Health — Console trace debugging & request-log sleuthing
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked the Altitude Health engineering team through the Console's tracing and request-log tools. Focus was on how to triage model errors, use request playback for debugging, and tie traces to SLOs. Security and private deployment constraints (KMS, SSO, VPC) were discussed and a plan for a 2-week pilot + benchmark was agreed.
next_steps: Priya to share Request Playback quickstart and link to tracing KB (by 2026-03-09)
Evan to send pilot quote and reserved capacity options (by 2026-03-10)
Altitude to provide sample failing request IDs and a short list of test prompts (by 2026-03-12)
action_items: Priya: Share console tracing step-by-step doc + demo recording (due 2026-03-09)
Evan: Put together 2-week pilot proposal with estimated token cost and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison (due 2026-03-10)
Sarah: Collect 10 noisy requests and send IDs to Redwood for replay (due 2026-03-12)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks; Priya Menon; Sarah Kim; Marco Ruiz; Nadia Khan

Summary/Highlights:
- Walkthrough of Console trace playback, request inspector, and request logs
- Demonstrated mapping of trace spans to token-level latency and where KV cache hits happen
- Discussed security: SSO, SC(looks like SOC)2, KMS/HSM, and VPC/private control plane
- Agreed pilot and follow-up actions

Topics covered: request playback, trace aggregation, sampling policies, error triage, batching tradeoffs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan: All right everyone, thanks for joining um let's do quick intros. I'm Evan from Redwood, account exec, and Priya is going to run the console walkthrough.
[00:19] Priya: Hi all. Thanks Sarah for setting this up. We'll start with a quick high level of the request flow and then jump into the Console: trace playback, request inspector, and how you can repro errors locally.
[00:35] Sarah: Sounds good. Quick note — our main pain is intermittent hallucinations in our triage assistant and then a spike in token cost on long sequences. We also have strict requirements for audit logs.
[00:50] Marco: And ops side, we need deterministic ways to reproduce bad outputs. Right now we get partial logs and it's not enough.
[01:05] Priya: Totally. That's what the Request Playback and the trace timeline are for — you can replay the exact request including KV cache state. A quick caveat, the KV cache — sometimes transcription shows it as "KV cash" in transcripts but it's cache — so we'll be clear.
[01:24] Nadia: Can you show the playback step? Like how do you capture the exact state?
[01:31] Priya: Yeah, give me a sec, I'm sharing my screen. 
[02:15] Priya: Ok on screen now, this is the Console. Over here we have the request list, you can filter by model, route, status code, token counts. I'm going to open a failing request from last week — note timestamps and the trace id at the top.
[03:02] Priya: The trace view shows spans for: request routing, kernel selection, kv-cache lookup, forward pass latency per layer, and post-processing. You can expand any span to see logs and metadata.
[03:30] Marco: That 'kernel selection' bit — is that coming from your runtime? It looks like hardware-specific metrics.
[03:39] Priya: Yeah that's from the serving runtime. We annotate spans with the chosen compute kernel and device. For Dedicated customers we can send more granular telemetry.
[03:52] Sarah: How do you show when a prefix hit the KV cache? We suspect a lot of our repeated prompts should be hitting but aren't.
[04:05] Priya: There's a CacheHit flag on the kv-cache span. In the Inspector you can also view the stored KV keys and TTL. Sometimes clients roll their prompts leading to mismatch keys.
[04:24] Evan: Also, on the request inspector we surface the prompt fingerprint — that helps de-duping. We'll share the KB with fingerprint examples.
[04:36] Nadia: The log snippet looks truncated — do you store raw request text in logs? We have PII concerns.
[04:46] Priya: Good question. By default we redact PII in logs at rest and we offer options: redact in transit, redact at ingest, or don't store raw prompts depending on contract. For Private deployments you can opt to keep raw logs behind your KMS.
[05:05] Sarah: SOC 2 is a must for us — do you have that?
[05:10] Evan: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We'll attach the compliance pack. We also have SAML SSO and role-based access in Console.
[05:22] Marco: What about KMS integration? We need HSM-backed key management.
[05:27] Priya: We support KMS + customer-managed HSM for Private. For hosted we integrate with cloud KMS but can also federate to customer HSM in Dedicated/private setups.
[05:40] Sarah: Great. Back to the trace. Show me how we isolate the token where hallucination started.
[05:48] Priya: Sure. If you expand the generation span you get per-token latency and logits snapshot. You can click 'view logits' — in some cases we include top-k tokens at each step. This helps see if the model jumped to a low-probability token unexpectedly.
[06:15] Nadia: Is logits view enabled by default, or does it affect cost?
[06:20] Priya: It's opt-in because it increases storage. For pilot we'll enable it on sampled requests.
[06:30] Evan: Also mention the Optimize suggestions — it can recommend quantization and batching profiles based on your token distribution, but we'll demo that later.
[06:42] Priya: Jumping ahead, here's a request where the client code retried and created duplicate prompt prefixes so the cache key was wrong. You can see two near-identical requests, one cache hit, one miss.
[07:05] Marco: Hmm, interesting. Can the Console correlate client-retry patterns with spikes in token cost?
[07:12] Priya: Yes — the per-route analytics show token usage over time and you can overlay cache hit rate. So you can spot when retries cause cost bumps.
[07:28] Sarah: If we wanted to replay a request but change a single header (e.g., user timezone) — can playback override request metadata?
[07:37] Priya: Yes, playback has an 'override' panel. You can change headers, session variables, even pin a model version. That shows you what would have happened without changing production traffic.
[07:51] Nadia: Are these replays hitting your production models or a sandbox?
[07:55] Priya: By default they run in an isolated replay lane that doesn't affect production telemetry. For high-fidelity we can spin up a matching environment in Dedicated for the pilot.
[08:08] Evan: Quick interjection — we often get asked about request-level RBAC. You can limit who can do replays in Console with roles.
[08:18] Marco: Nice. Can you show an example of a trace that ends with a 5xx and how to triage?
[08:27] Priya: Sure, opening an error trace now. See the failure span: it's a tensor allocation spike before the kernel call, then OOM on device. The trace shows memory pressure and fallback to CPU.
[08:45] Marco: Does Redwood surface GC/allocator metrics?
[08:49] Priya: For Dedicated yes; for hosted we show high-level memory signals and automatic fallback events.
[08:58] Sarah: We need SLA around fallback behavior — like auto-retry vs immediate 5xx.
[09:05] Evan: That's configurable in routing policies. We can do automatic fallback to a lighter quantized variant or queue for retry depending on your SLOs.
[09:18] Nadia: About sampling — do you sample traces or capture all?
[09:22] Priya: Sampling is configurable. By default we sample all errors and a percentage of successes per route. You can bump sampling for routes you care about.
[09:32] Sarah: For compliance, we need immutable audit logs for a year — is that supported?
[09:38] Priya: Yes, audit log retention is configurable. For Private you'll manage retention behind your storage; for hosted we offer retention tiers.
[09:48] Evan: Quick note on integrations — we can forward trace alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or your internal SRE tools.
[09:56] Marco: Can we pull traces into our existing APM?
[10:00] Priya: Absolutely, we have exporters for Zipkin/Jaeger-compatible formats and OTLP.
[10:12] Sarah: Okay, let's do a live replay of that failing request you mentioned and tweak the cache key.
[10:18] Priya: Kicking off replay — note the log window — it's capturing the exact request payload. I'm going to edit the prompt fingerprint to force a cache hit. Replay results: when we force the correct fingerprint you see latency drop from ~420ms to ~120ms and the generation is stable.
[10:42] Nadia: That's helpful. One concern — if we store some raw prompts for debugging, how do we ensure PII isn't leaked in daily ops?
[10:50] Priya: We can set up an automated scrubber and only surface redacted snippets in the Console list, while raw text is stored encrypted with your KMS where you control access.
[11:05] Marco: What about network egress and data residency? We need EU-only processing for certain flows.
[11:12] Evan: We have regional routing and can route EU requests to EU infrastructure. For Private we can do full on-prem.
[11:21] Sarah: Any examples of customers using request-playback for compliance audits?
[11:27] Priya: Yes, we've worked with a couple of healthcare customers; they kept replay artifacts behind customer-managed storage and used the console for triage only.
[11:36] Evan: Quick sidebar: competitors like Pinecone get mentioned mostly for vector ops; Redwood focuses on inference serving + traceability.
[11:48] Sarah: Cool. On the playback UI, can we bulk tag requests for later analysis?
[11:53] Priya: Yes you can bulk select and tag or export to CSV.
[12:00] Nadia: Let's talk about performance debugging — if a specific layer is slow, can Console show layer-level timing?
[12:07] Priya: Yep, per-layer timings are surfaced when available from the runtime. And you can compare across traces to find regressions.
[12:18] Marco: How do you handle versioned models? If we rollout a new variant, can we A/B and then fallback automatically?
[12:25] Priya: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. The Console shows per-model variant metrics.
[12:35] Sarah: If we do a pilot, what telemetry level do you recommend? Full trace for errors and 10% success sampling?
[12:44] Priya: That's a common pattern — sample all errors + 10% successes, enable logits on sampled traces. We'll help tune it based on your traffic.
[12:56] Evan: Let's switch to an example where a downstream parser caused unexpected tokenization leading to hallucination.
[13:02] Priya: Opening trace: you can see pre-processing span where tokenization delta happened. It shows a mismatched encoding- our client used utf-16 in one code path.
[13:18] Nadia: Oh wow. That'd break the fingerprinting.
[13:21] Priya: Exactly. Console's request inspector stores the effective input bytes so you can spot encoding mismatches.
[13:30] Marco: Regarding cost optimization, you mentioned batching earlier — how does batching interact with latency-sensitive routes?
[13:36] Priya: You can set per-route batching thresholds and max-latency SLO. The runtime will batch only when it doesn't violate per-request SLOs. Optimize then suggests batch sizes by analyzing your token length distribution.
[13:55] Sarah: For pilot, can we run a cost baseline report?
[14:00] Evan: Yes we'll run a baseline with your sample traces and show potential savings with caching and batching.
[14:08] Priya: Back to the trace: here's a case where a quantized variant produced a subtle factual error. In the Console we can run side-by-side model comparisons for the same request.
[14:25] Nadia: Side-by-side is great. That could be part of our evaluation criteria.
[14:30] Priya: I'm going to create a short saved view — filters, tags, and a preconfigured comparison. You can share these with teammates.
[14:45] Marco: Can saved views be shared across teams with RBAC?
[14:49] Priya: Yes, they can be published to your org and controlled by roles.
[15:00] Evan: Quick pause for parking lot items- Sarah asked for SOC 2 docs, we'll send those. Also pilot pricing and a short benchmark plan.
[15:12] Sarah: Good. Let's move toward an ops example: we had a sustained period of 503s last month, want to see how Redwood would surface that.
[15:20] Priya: Opening the incident timeline view — it aggregates errors, annotations, and trace links. You can jump from incident into the exact failing request.
[15:34] Sarah: If an incident is triggered, can it auto-open a ticket in JIRA?
[15:38] Priya: Yes we have integrations to auto-create issues with trace links and context.
[15:45] Nadia: Request retention: how long are traces and logs kept by default?
[15:50] Priya: Default is 90 days for traces in hosted; you can extend with retention tiers. For Private you configure retention.
[15:58] Marco: For our SREs, exporting traces in OTLP to our central observability is key.
[16:03] Priya: We'll set up an OTLP export and ensure trace IDs map to your correlation ID.
[16:12] Evan: We're about 1/3 through- want to do a short live-fix demo where we patch client fingerprinting?
[16:19] Sarah: Yes please, that's our key blocker.
[16:25] Priya: Demo: I open the failing request, show the fingerprint mismatch, then edit the client code snippet in the Console's inline debugger — note this is for demo only, you wouldn't edit production in Console. Then we re-run replay and you can see the cache hit.
[16:50] Marco: That's useful. How would this look in a Private deployment?
[16:55] Priya: Same Console UI but control plane can be customer-managed. For playbacks we can run replays inside customer's VPC.
[17:05] Nadia: A couple of micro speech artifacts — your transcripts sometimes spell Redwood product names weirdly in our notes as 'Red wood' or 'Redwood Opti-ma' — just FYI.
[17:14] Priya: Ha, yeah automatic transcripts do weird things. We'll share a clean recording.
[17:22] Sarah: On security, Marco asked about access to raw logs — who on Redwood can ever read them?
[17:28] Evan: Access is strictly controlled; for hosted there are break-glass controls and audit logs whenever Redwood support accesses data. For Private, you manage access. We'll include the access matrix in the SOC2 package.
[17:40] Priya: Switching to a question from Nadia on alerting thresholds — you can set anomaly detectors for token-burn or latency and configure thresholds per route.
[17:50] Nadia: Can anomaly detectors train on our historical traffic?
[17:53] Priya: They can be fed your historical traces; we also provide rule-based alerts out of the box.
[18:02] Marco: Any rate limits on replays? If we wanted to replay 10k requests for an investigation?
[18:09] Priya: For hosted there are quotas per account. For Dedicated/Private we can scale replay capacity. Large-scale replays we'd coordinate to avoid thundering herd on model endpoints.
[18:24] Sarah: Let's go back to the example where model fallback caused skew in outputs. Can the Console surface when a request fell back to a cheaper quantized model?
[18:33] Priya: Yes, the trace includes the executed model variant. You can filter by fallback events and then compare outputs.
[18:42] Nadia: Do you preserve sampling of outputs for A/B comparisons over time?
[18:46] Priya: We keep sampled outputs according to your retention settings so you can do longitudinal comparisons.
[18:55] Evan: We usually recommend setting up a prompt-eval suite and tying regressions to alerts; Optimize can run these evals and push alerts on drift.
[19:07] Sarah: Can Optimize plug into our CI for pre-deploy checks?
[19:11] Priya: Yes, Optimize has an API for eval runs you can include in CI.
[19:18] Marco: For the pilot we want to validate 3 things: reproducible replays, per-token traceability, and cost improvement.
[19:27] Evan: Noted. We'll make pilot success criteria and include regression checks.
[19:33] Priya: I'm going to demo a saved trace workflow: tag as 'hallucination', add notes, and schedule a replay job. Then create a compare view between the current model and a quantized candidate.
[19:47] Nadia: If we find regression in the quantized variant, can Console automatically open a rollback?
[19:52] Priya: You can set auto-fallback but rollbacks are manual — we recommend canary plus auto-fallback on error thresholds.
[20:02] Marco: Any gotchas for fingerprinting when dealing with non-deterministic prompt assembly across microservices?
[20:09] Priya: Yes - centralizing prompt assembly or using canonicalization libraries helps. Console's fingerprinting works best when you canonicalize whitespace and metadata.
[20:20] Sarah: Let's talk timelines — we'd like to kick a pilot next week. Is that feasible?
[20:25] Evan: We can start onboarding in a week for hosted pilot; dedicated setup takes longer. We'll scope required telemetry and sample data.
[20:35] Priya: For the onboarding we'll need sample requests, a small test dataset, and a short doc of what to measure.
[20:42] Sarah: We'll prepare those.
[20:45] Priya: Jumping ahead to an example from ops: here's a trace with intermittent latency spikes. In the timeline you can correlate GC events on the host with latency.
[21:00] Marco: Do you correlate infra metrics from our cloud provider?
[21:05] Priya: We can ingest external metrics and overlay them on the trace timeline so you see host-level metrics beside per-token timings.
[21:16] Nadia: About export formats — CSV for logs, OTLP for traces, and raw JSON for full export?
[21:21] Priya: Yes to all.
[21:27] Sarah: If we run the pilot and decide to go Dedicated later, can we migrate data and configs?
[21:34] Evan: Yes we support migration paths and config export/import. We'll include migration runbook in the pilot package.
[21:44] Marco: Any limitations on model types for trace detail? e.g., some open models expose less telemetry?
[21:51] Priya: Telemetry granularity can vary by model and runtime. We surface what the runtime provides; we also add synthetic spans where needed.
[22:02] Nadia: Let's capture the meeting questions so we don't miss anything.
[22:06] Evan: Good idea. (They recap aloud)
[22:15] Sarah: Who owns replay artifacts in Hosted?
[22:18] Priya: Redwood stores them but access controlled, and audit logs show any access.
[22:25] Sarah: Ok. Next, any final security clarifications?
[22:29] Evan: We'll attach the SOC2 and our data processing addendum.
[22:35] Marco: Fine.
[22:38] Priya: I'm going to finish with a short checklist for pilot: sample dataset ingestion, enable error trace sampling, enable playback for sample traces, and schedule a follow-up check-in.
[22:52] Sarah: That's perfect.
[23:00] Evan: Wrapping up — Priya and I will push docs and pilot pricing. We also asked Sarah to send sample request IDs.
[23:12] Sarah: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[23:20] Priya: Quick QA — does anyone want a side-by-side of two traces now?
[23:25] Nadia: Not needed now, recording will help.
[23:30] Evan: Great. End of demo.
[23:35] // Closing chatter and hold music in recording 

Note: timestamps above are approximate; the full recording and exported transcript (clean) will be shared.
